messages:
sanjay: quick flag - sablev2-int4 canary shows weird enum/id collisions in function outputs on the backend batch. noticed after the latest quant pass.
canary-bot: canary=sablev2-int4 subset=api-toolcalls structural_errors=1.1% -> 6.9% (12h)
rita: examples?
sanjay: pasting a few raw model emits from the canary logs (trimmed):
```
{"action": 2, "params": {"filePath": "/tmp/log.txt", "mode": "w"}}
{"action": "2", "params": "{\"filePath\":\"/tmp/notes.md\",\"mode\":\"a\"}"}
{"action": "save_file", "params": ["/tmp/out.txt", "content here"]}
{"action": null, "params": {"path": "/tmp/x"}}
```
sanjay: schema expects action to be one of ["save_file","append","delete"], and params to be an object with explicit keys. now we get numeric codes, strings, arrays, or nulls. parser rejects these.
lee: so failures are type/shape mismatches, not parsing per se. but our router treats those as parse failures since they break the call contract.
emily: does this correlate with prompt language or length?
sanjay: mostly short system prompts with non-English examples in a few spots. but also some english-only tickets. signal stronger after int4 vs fp16.
nate: could this be tokenization aliasing causing enum tokens to be emitted as ids? e.g., model learned to map "2" -> append in some training data and quantization changed token split.
rita: interesting - also saw nested params occasionally become array form when model tries to be succinct. maybe beam/temperature interaction exacerbates.
emily: mitigation ideas: 1) soft-schema enforcement in prompt (canonical example), 2) post-emit type coercer (map numeric -> enum via lookup), 3) small discriminator model to accept/reject before invoking heavy fallback.
lee: runtime cost matters. post-emit coercion cheap: if action is int or string-digit map using enum_map = {"1":"save_file","2":"append","3":"delete"}. that would fix ~60% of cases in sample.
nate: for arrays-as-params, we can try heuristics: if params is list and length==2 assume [path,content] -> convert to object. but risk of false positives.
sanjay: we should quantify regressions per-class. canary dataset -> run a parsing-coverage breakdown: parse_error_type=[numeric-action,stringified-json,array-params,null-missing]. emily can you add this to nightly?
emily: yep will add a fine-grained metric and graph it. will run the int4 set + fp16 baseline.
rita: if coercions recover >85% with low false positive we can ship int4 with runtime repair. otherwise we keep these endpoints on fp16.
ate: also asking the quant team: try a pass with larger bias-preserve clipping or adjust per-token scale. maybe the enum tokens are low-probability under the int4 mapping.
sanjay: action list: emily add detailed parse-type metrics; lee prototype enum_map + array->object coercer on canary pipeline; rita coordinate with quant for a bias-preserve PTQ run. report tomorrow noon.
lee: I'll put a tiny PR to the canary postprocessor and run A/B. low-risk.
rita: tagging @canary-bot action too: mark samples where coercer changed payload so we can inspect regressions.
sanjay: thanks team. feel free to ping on thread with short updates. :rocket:
